issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Institutional Failure: The people or institutions that should have protected me let me down
issues.explanation: For a mugging/robbery trauma, 'Institutional Failure' is hard to justify unless there is additional context about police, employers, or security personnel failing him; nothing else in the profile supports that theme, so this appraisal appears disconnected from the trauma type and the rest of the formulation.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Lost Community: I have lost my connection to my community and culture
issues.explanation: 'Lost Community' is also weakly anchored to a single mugging/robbery and is not supported by the other selected items; it suggests a broader social/cultural rupture that is not reflected in triggers, threat, or memory content.

issues.item: Threat: Threat in Silence: Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen
issues.explanation: 'Threat in Silence' is more suggestive of ongoing ambient danger or interpersonal abuse contexts; with the current trigger set (nightmares, fatigue, physical locations) and robbery trauma, it lacks a clear clinical bridge and feels insufficiently tied to the rest of the profile.

vignette:
Arjun, a 29-year-old painter from a South Asian background, found himself ensnared in a web of anxiety and fear following a traumatic mugging last year. The incident had left an indelible mark on him. He vividly recalled the evening when he was walking home from a late job, paintbrushes still tucked under his arm, when a group of men confronted him. The memory of that confrontation loomed heavily in his mind, making every shadow and every unfamiliar figure on the street feel like an imminent threat, as if danger could strike again at any moment. He remembered the rush of adrenaline, the fear coursing through his veins as they demanded his wallet and phone. The ordeal lasted mere minutes, but it felt like an eternity, and he would wake up in a cold sweat, haunted by nightmares of the event—dreams where he relived the moment again and again, the panic rising in his chest as he struggled to break free. Each time he awoke, he felt a surge of irritability, an angry outburst bubbling just beneath the surface. It was as if he had become a stranger to himself, his body always on high alert, constantly scanning his surroundings for potential threats. 

The physical locations where the mugging had occurred became charged with anxiety. The memories flooding back in those places carried a palpable sense of danger, as if the threat he had once faced was still lurking just out of sight, making each return feel like an invitation to experience fear anew. Each encounter with these reminders intensified the feeling of danger, causing Arjun's heartbeat to quicken and his breath to shorten, as if the threat of the mugging was reawakening within him, ready to strike again. Each time he encountered these reminders of his trauma, he found himself thinking that this was what his life had become — an endless cycle of fear and vulnerability that he could never escape. Simply passing by those streets triggered a rush of intrusive memories, causing his heart to race and his palms to sweat. These memories flooded back with such intensity that they felt alive, forcing him to relive the fear and vulnerability of the event as if it were happening anew, amplifying his sense of threat. These moments magnified the tense state his body had adopted; he felt as if he were perpetually ready to react to danger, a sensation that transformed his daily life into a battleground. The memories that surfaced in those moments only served to heighten his sense of danger, making him feel as though he was back in the confrontation, every detail sharp and close, reinforcing his belief that he was under constant threat. The world outside was a constant reminder of his trauma, and each spatial trigger intensified his belief that he could no longer trust the people around him. Each time he encountered these triggers, his body would react with a surge of fear, amplifying the sense of threat that loomed over him, as if danger was not just a memory but a present reality. He had come to mistrust everyone, convinced that anyone could become a threat, and this growing isolation made him feel more detached from those he loved. His certainty that he was always at risk led him to interpret even innocent interactions as potential betrayals, reinforcing the belief that he could not trust anyone. This belief that he was a target, not just unlucky, but chosen, made every new situation feel like a test he was destined to fail, amplifying the sense of threat that permeated his daily life. This deep-seated belief that he was always vulnerable led him to interpret every interaction with others as a potential source of danger, making him more anxious and guarded in social situations. His negative beliefs about his own safety shaped how he viewed the world, instilling a persistent sense of danger that made him hyper-aware of any situation where he might feel exposed or vulnerable. Having come to believe that he was always at risk, Arjun approached even the most mundane interactions with an underlying tension, bracing himself for potential threats that existed only in his mind. 

As he grappled with these feelings, Arjun found it difficult to piece together the memory of the mugging. Yet, whenever those fragmented memories surfaced, they were accompanied by a crushing sense of immediacy, leading him to feel as if the danger of that night was still very much alive, echoing within him. After those memories broke through, Arjun would find himself grappling with the thought that if he kept reliving the trauma, it confirmed a deeper flaw within himself, reinforcing his negative self-appraisals and enhancing the threat he felt from the world around him. Every time those memories broke through, he couldn’t shake the thought that if he kept reliving the trauma, it only confirmed his fear that he was weak and unworthy of safety. He often felt as though he was only recalling fragments of the experience, the gaps gnawing at him and fueling his guilt. Each time those fragments emerged, he couldn't help but think they revealed a deep flaw within himself, reinforcing his belief that he was weak and unworthy of safety, which further fueled his anxiety about future threats. Once those memories broke through, they amplified his sense of danger, as if the past were still alive within him, creating an ever-present anxiety that made it hard to feel secure anywhere. The flashbacks left him feeling hunted in his own home, as though the danger had not receded into memory but had instead taken up residence within him, ready to pounce at any moment. Each time those fragments surfaced, they deepened his conviction that he had failed to protect himself, reinforcing his belief that he was inadequate and leaving him feeling hopeless and trapped. He would sit in his studio, attempting to deliberate on the event, but the harder he tried to access the painful recollections, the more elusive they became. This incomplete picture of the traumatic event compounded his feelings of guilt; he often questioned why he hadn’t fought back or run faster, which only deepened his sense of inadequacy. The memories, though fragmented, remained potent triggers—each recall would send him spiraling back into that moment of vulnerability, enhancing his sense of danger and leading him to believe that he was incapable of relying on anyone, not even himself.

Arjun's negative appraisals shaped his perception of the world, creating a vicious cycle. His mistrust of people steered him towards isolation, which only fortified his belief that he couldn’t rely on others. As he withdrew from social interactions, he would find himself alone in his thoughts, the memories of the mugging replaying in his mind, reinforcing his feelings of vulnerability. The threat he felt was not just from the memories themselves; it seeped into every aspect of his life, making even casual encounters feel like potential ambushes, further pushing him into isolation. This heightened sense of threat made him hyper-vigilant, as he began to perceive danger in ordinary situations, each unexpected sound or glance confirming his belief that he was constantly in peril. This constant reflection contributed to his irritability and made him more sensitive to perceived slights from others, aggravating his readiness to react defensively. With an ever-present sense of threat, even minor interactions felt charged; he interpreted casual remarks as veiled attacks, convinced that others were judging him, and this only solidified his desire to withdraw further into isolation. His memories of the traumatic event seemed to taunt him, leading him to interpret innocent interactions as threats, convinced that others were judging him or harboring malicious intent. Each day became a struggle as he navigated through the layers of his trauma, caught in an ever-tightening loop of anxiety and avoidance.

When Arjun finally sought help, he felt a glimmer of hope mixed with the fear of confronting his trauma. He was acutely aware that the memories he carried would not only resurface but could also amplify his fears, making every session feel like stepping into a minefield of emotions he had long tried to avoid. He harbored a deep-seated worry that delving into his memories would only serve to amplify his feelings of guilt and mistrust, but he knew he could not continue living in this state of hypervigilance. He longed to reclaim the joy he once found in painting, to reconnect with his wife and friends without the shadow of his trauma looming overhead. Yet, he feared that engaging with those memories would only serve to reinforce his belief that he was permanently broken, trapped in a cycle of pain and mistrust that he couldn't escape. With each session, he hoped to find a way to unravel the knots of his experience, to understand the connection between the past and present, and to ultimately heal from the scars that had come to define his daily existence.

vignette_attempts.feedback:
REQUIRED EDGES MISSING:
- Triggers → Threat: The vignette does not establish a causal relationship where triggers lead to a sense of threat.
  e.g. "The cues led to a feeling of danger that felt as real as the original event."
  e.g. "A knock at the door after dark sent her heart into her throat — her body read it as an emergency, even when her mind knew better."
  e.g. "Sitting in the waiting room, she noticed a man watching her from across the room and felt the same cold certainty: something terrible was about to happen."
- Triggers → Memory: The vignette does not establish a causal relationship where triggers lead to memory.
  e.g. "The smell of his cologne in the lift sent the whole night flooding back before she had even reached her floor."
  e.g. "Hearing that song on the radio dragged her straight back into the room where it happened, as if no time had passed at all."
  e.g. "Walking past the bus stop where it occurred, she was no longer on the street — she was back there, every detail sharp and close."
- Negative Appraisals → Threat: The vignette does not establish a causal relationship where negative appraisals lead to a sense of threat.
  e.g. "Having decided that she was permanently vulnerable, she walked into rooms already braced — the threat arrived with her before anything had happened."
  e.g. "The belief that she was a target — not unlucky, but chosen — meant that every unfamiliar face carried a weight of potential danger."
  e.g. "Her certainty that she couldn't protect herself made every new situation feel like a test she was already failing."
- Negative Appraisals → Triggers: The vignette does not establish a causal relationship where negative appraisals lead to triggers.
  e.g. "Once she had concluded that the world was fundamentally unsafe, almost anything could confirm it — a figure in her periphery, the wrong tone of voice, footsteps behind her."
  e.g. "The belief that she couldn't trust her own judgement meant that things she would once have registered and dismissed now snagged and held her attention."
  e.g. "Her conviction that it would happen again meant she moved through ordinary days as if they were mined — every ambiguity became a potential signal."
- Memory → Threat: The vignette does not establish a causal relationship where memory leads to a sense of threat.
  e.g. "Once the memory had surfaced, she couldn't shake the sense that the danger was still present — that it had simply moved into her body rather than gone away."
  e.g. "The flashback left her standing in her own kitchen feeling hunted, even with the door locked and the lights on."
  e.g. "After the memory broke through, the threat felt immediate and physical — not something that had happened, but something that was still happening."
- Memory → Negative Appraisals: The vignette does not establish a causal relationship where memory leads to negative appraisals.
  e.g. "After the image broke through again, she caught herself thinking: if this keeps happening, there must be something deeply wrong with me."
  e.g. "The memory surfaced in the middle of a meeting and she spent the rest of the day convinced that everyone around her could see how broken she was."
  e.g. "Each time the flashback came, the thought that followed it was always the same — that she had let this happen, and that it said something permanent about who she was."
- Memory → Triggers: The vignette does not establish a causal relationship where memory leads to triggers.
  e.g. "After the memory had surfaced, even the most ordinary things — a kettle whistling, a door slamming — felt like warnings she couldn't afford to ignore."
  e.g. "The intrusive image left her scanning every room she entered, cataloguing exits, tracking faces, unable to switch off."
  e.g. "Because the memory came back so vividly, she began to see threads of it everywhere: in strangers' faces, in certain times of day, in the quality of winter light."
- Threat → Triggers: The vignette does not establish a causal relationship where threat leads to triggers.
  e.g. "Already running on threat, she found that almost anything could tip into a warning — a van parked at an odd angle, a light left on that shouldn't have been."
  e.g. "The background hum of danger she carried everywhere made ordinary cues feel like messages — each one confirming what her body already believed."
  e.g. "Living at that pitch of alertness, she found the world had become dense with reminders she couldn't stop reading."

vignette_attempts.vignette:
Arjun, a 29-year-old painter from a South Asian background, found himself ensnared in a web of anxiety and fear following a traumatic mugging last year. The incident had left an indelible mark on him. He vividly recalled the evening when he was walking home from a late job, paintbrushes still tucked under his arm, when a group of men confronted him. The memory of that confrontation loomed heavily in his mind, making every shadow and every unfamiliar figure on the street feel like an imminent threat, as if danger could strike again at any moment. He remembered the rush of adrenaline, the fear coursing through his veins as they demanded his wallet and phone. The ordeal lasted mere minutes, but it felt like an eternity, and he would wake up in a cold sweat, haunted by nightmares of the event—dreams where he relived the moment again and again, the panic rising in his chest as he struggled to break free. Each time he awoke, he felt a surge of irritability, an angry outburst bubbling just beneath the surface. It was as if he had become a stranger to himself, his body always on high alert, constantly scanning his surroundings for potential threats. 

The physical locations where the mugging had occurred became charged with anxiety. The memories flooding back in those places carried a palpable sense of danger, as if the threat he had once faced was still lurking just out of sight, making each return feel like an invitation to experience fear anew. Simply passing by those streets triggered a rush of intrusive memories, causing his heart to race and his palms to sweat. These memories flooded back with such intensity that they felt alive, forcing him to relive the fear and vulnerability of the event as if it were happening anew, amplifying his sense of threat. These moments magnified the tense state his body had adopted; he felt as if he were perpetually ready to react to danger, a sensation that transformed his daily life into a battleground. The memories that surfaced in those moments only served to heighten his sense of danger, making him feel as though he was back in the confrontation, every detail sharp and close, reinforcing his belief that he was under constant threat. The world outside was a constant reminder of his trauma, and each spatial trigger intensified his belief that he could no longer trust the people around him. Each time he encountered these triggers, his body would react with a surge of fear, amplifying the sense of threat that loomed over him, as if danger was not just a memory but a present reality. He had come to mistrust everyone, convinced that anyone could become a threat, and this growing isolation made him feel more detached from those he loved. This deep-seated belief that he was always vulnerable led him to interpret every interaction with others as a potential source of danger, making him more anxious and guarded in social situations. His negative beliefs about his own safety shaped how he viewed the world, instilling a persistent sense of danger that made him hyper-aware of any situation where he might feel exposed or vulnerable. Having come to believe that he was always at risk, Arjun approached even the most mundane interactions with an underlying tension, bracing himself for potential threats that existed only in his mind.

He often felt as though he was only recalling fragments of the experience, the gaps gnawing at him and fueling his guilt. Each time those fragments surfaced, they deepened his conviction that he had failed to protect himself, reinforcing his belief that he was inadequate and leaving him feeling hopeless and trapped. He would sit in his studio, attempting to deliberate on the event, but the harder he tried to access the painful recollections, the more elusive they became. This incomplete picture of the traumatic event compounded his feelings of guilt; he often questioned why he hadn’t fought back or run faster, which only deepened his sense of inadequacy.
